1.label: very_easy
1.summary: Deliver one short request with a slowly turning globe and a wide dish-aim tolerance; one visible station can complete it without a handoff.
1.natural_language: Aim one station at the requested spacecraft and keep its relay alive until the short transfer completes.

2.label: easy
2.summary: Deliver two requests. The globe turns slowly enough that each link normally completes, but the operator must select a station that is above the current horizon.
2.natural_language: Use the three ground stations to complete both spacecraft requests; aim each visible dish and hold the relay.

3.label: medium
3.summary: Maintain the current three-request relay. Three-dimensional latitude and depth determine which station is above each spacecraft's local horizon, and an aim must be refreshed before the rotating planet drifts it out of tolerance.
3.natural_language: Read the rotating 3D globe, aim a visible station at each requested spacecraft, keep each transfer moving, and hand off before a horizon loss.

4.label: hard
4.summary: Complete four requests with faster rotation, tighter aim tolerance, and a wider spread of orbital latitudes. Keeping the dish aligned now requires repeated visual corrections and more deliberate handoffs.
4.natural_language: Coordinate all four relays across changing station horizons. Re-aim as the globe turns and hand off every transfer before its current station loses line of sight.

5.label: very_hard
5.summary: Coordinate five requests while the planet turns quickly. Tight pointing, broad 3D latitude variation, and longer transfers make station choice and recovery from a lost link part of the same plan.
5.natural_language: Complete the five spacecraft deliveries with continuous visual re-aiming and timely station handoffs; no request may be abandoned.

simplified.summary: Choose a station and spacecraft with visible buttons, then press HOLD LINK; the same globe, requests, visibility, progress, and handoff rules remain active.

full.summary: Drag a visible station dish directly to a spacecraft marker to aim and start a link; drag again to re-aim or hand off as the globe turns.
